items: Major adaptive jumps are proposed to arise when active structural constraints are crossed, especially representation boundaries, expanding reachable adaptive/computational regimes.
Gradual improvement is distinguished from structural phase transition; closed fixed-representation saturation is distinguished from open representation/operator/regime expansion.
Delta Lambda_E -> Delta alpha -> Delta C; proposed strong transition signature Delta D_R*>0, Delta C_R>0, Delta A>0.
Definitions for evolutionary constraint boundary, accessible regime, capability, information/representation/computational/observation boundaries and reachable computational space.
Illustrations include compute-with-fixed-representation, deep learning, AlphaZero and scientific method.
Candidate phase-transition measurements track capability, adaptive representation, permeability and reachable computation deltas.
Source relates ASEB phase-boundary mechanics to Ancestor Intelligence selection of future-evolution-expanding transitions; endpoint unresolved.
What measurable structural changes cause adaptive systems to cross into new evolutionary regimes?
Thresholds, overlapping bottlenecks, variable estimators, historical causal attribution, measurement validity, strong-transition sufficiency and endpoint identity remain unresolved.
Formal variables are explicitly candidate hypotheses, not fixed laws.
Candidate adaptive-state, horizon, permeability, D_R*, O_G+, ancestor-signature and phase-boundary structures.

Definitions for adaptive-state components, five adaptation depths, four resolution horizons, permeability components, operator generation, evolutionary fertility and quality-weighted future branching.
Stable adaptation is proposed to require nonzero permeability; future adaptive capacity is proposed to depend on creating new ways of adapting.
Predictions: capability can rise without fertility; major transitions involve representation/operator expansion; fertility predicts stronger long-term growth than immediate performance alone.
Can candidate variables be operationalized, predict adaptation, identify phase transitions and support artificial fertility objectives?
System mapping, depth criteria, horizon/permeability/D_R*/O_G+/F_A/B_F*/dependency/phase metrics and absent empirical tests remain unresolved.
Hypotheses aim to distinguish ASEB from simpler compute, optimization, information and performance explanations rather than prove it.

Eight hypotheses cover capability-vs-fertility divergence, representation expansion, operator generation, constraint-crossing phase boundaries, permeability, ancestor independence, evolutionary closure under intelligence growth, and fertility objectives for open-ended evolution.
Examples include fixed-task optimized models, language/math/programming transitions, representation-limited systems and scientific/programming/math/education ancestor candidates.

Falsification and proposed tests compare capability vs fertility, representation change, reusable operators, horizon constraints, permeability, dependency, fitness+fertility objectives and three minimal benchmarks.
Highly optimized systems may require explicit preservation of epistemic/ontological permeability to avoid closure.
Outcome scope, D_R*/O_G+/horizon/permeability/dependency/F_A metrics, compression mechanism, reward/scalarization, executable protocols and absent results remain unresolved.
Do future-capacity-expanding systems outperform systems optimizing current objectives?
Current capability A_t is contrasted with future adaptive capacity F_A; Task->Performance benchmark is contrasted with Environment->{Performance,FutureCapacity}.

Six prospective experiments cover fertility-vs-fitness, operator discovery, representation expansion, permeability stress, ancestor removal and phase-boundary detection, with candidate D_R*/O_G+/B_F* metrics and support/partial/failure outcome categories.

Predictions include long-horizon fertility advantage, compounding reusable-operator returns, representation-expansion advantage under unknown structure, open-system advantage across regime changes, and nonlinear phase transitions.
Illustration contrasts isolated task solution with reusable operator generating multiple solutions.
A is current task performance; Dependency_t is future capability dependence on the original system.
ASEB is explicitly framed as an empirical hypothesis rather than vocabulary alone.
Strong evidence would predict transitions before occurrence; deepest advantage is proposed as creation of future adaptive capacity and increasingly deep improvement mechanisms.
F_A objective, experiment controls, metrics, threshold/discontinuity criteria, proxy validity and absent executable/results surface remain unresolved.
